heading: Name and Nature of the Association
text: The name of the Association shall be The Villas At Worthington Homeowners Association, Inc., and shall be an Ohio nonprofit limited liability company.

heading: Membership
text: Each owner upon acquisition of title to a Lot shall automatically become a member of the Association. Such Membership shall terminate upon the sale or other disposition by such Member of his or her Lot ownership, at which time the new Owner of such Lot shall automatically become a Member of the Association.

heading: Definitions
text: The terms used in this Code of Regulations shall have the same meaning as set forth in the Declaration, unless the context shall prohibit. Article II — Meetings of Members

heading: Place of Meetings
text: Meetings of the Association shall be held at the principal office of the Association or at such other suitable place convenient to the Members as may be designated by the Board of Directors either in North Royalton, Cuyahoga County, Ohio or as convenient thereto as possible and practical.

heading: Annual Meetings
text: The first meeting of the Members, whether a regular or special meeting, shall be held within one (1) year from the date of incorporation of the Association. The next annual meeting shall be set by the Board so as to occur no later than thirty (30) days before the close of the Association’s fiscal year. Subsequent annual meetings of the Members shall be held within thirty (30) days of the same day of the same month of each year thereafter at an hour set by the Board. The annual meeting of the Members shall be held at a date and time as set by the Board.

heading: Special Meetings
text: The President may call special meetings. In addition, it shall be the duty of the President to call special meetings of the Association if so directed by resolution of a majority of a quorum of the Board of Directors or a written petition signed by at least twenty-five (25%) percent of the total votes of the Association. The notice of special meetings shall state the date, time and place of such meeting and the purpose thereof. No business shall be transacted at special meetings except as stated in the notice.

heading: Notice of Meetings
text: It shall be the duty of the Secretary to cause to be delivered to the Owner of record of each Lot a notice of each annual or special meetings of the Association stating the purpose of the special meetings, as well as the time and place where it is to be held. Notice shall be given in accordance with Article VII, Section 7. Notices for meetings of the Members shall be served not less than ten (10) nor more than sixty (60) days before a meeting.

heading: Waiver of Notice
text: Waiver of notice of a meeting of the Members shall be deemed the equivalent of proper notice. Any Member may, in writing, waive notice of any meeting of the Members, either before or after the holding of such meeting. Attendance of any Member at any meeting without protesting, prior to or at the commencement of the meeting, the lack of proper notice shall be deemed to be a waiver by him or her of such meeting.

heading: Adjournment of Meetings
text: If any meetings of the Association cannot be held because a quorum is not present, a majority of the Members who are present at such meeting, either in person or by proxy, may adjourn the meeting to a time not less than five (5) nor more than thirty (30) days from the time the original meeting was called. At such adjourned meeting at which a quorum is present, any business which might have been transacted at the meeting originally called may be transacted. If a time and place of the adjourned meeting are not fixed by those in attendance at the original meeting, or if for any reason a new date is fixed for the adjourned meeting after adjournment, notice of the time and place of the adjourned meeting shall be given to Members in the manner prescribed for regular meetings. Those present at a duly called or held meeting at which a quorum is present may continue to do business until adjournment, notwithstanding the withdrawal of enough Members to leave less than a quorum, provided that any action taken shall be approved by at least a majority of Members required to constitute a quorum.

heading: Voting Rights
text: Each Lot shall have one vote. If only one of several Owners for a Lot is present at a meeting of the Association, that Owner is entitled to cast the vote allocated to that Lot. If more than one of the Owners is present, the vote allocated to that Lot may be cast only in accordance with the agreement of a majority in interest of the Owners. There is majority agreement if any one of the Owners casts a vote allocated to that Lot without protest being made promptly to the person presiding over the meeting by any of the other Owners of the Lot. The Association may adopt rules regarding deadlocks. No votes allocated to a Lot owned by the Association may be cast. Unless expressly reserved and the Association is notified of such reservation, a land contract vendee as defined in Chapter 5313 of the Revised Code, shall be deemed the proxy of a land contract vendor for purposes of this section.

heading: Proxies
text: A vote allocated to a Lot may be cast pursuant to a proxy duly executed by an Owner. If a Lot is owned by more than one person, each Owner of the Lot may vote or register protest to the casting of votes by the Owners of a Lot through a duly executed proxy. An Owner may revoke a proxy given pursuant to this section only by actual notice of revocation to the person presiding over a meeting of the Association. A proxy is void if it is not dated or purports to be revocable without notice. Except as hereinafter provided, a proxy shall terminate one year after its date, unless it specifies a shorter time. If a first mortgagee has been designated a proxy under the terms of a first mortgage covering the Lot, its presentation to the Board of a copy of the mortgage shall be notice of the proxy designation, and if the mortgage so states, of the irrevocability of that designation. Written notice to the Board or notice in a meeting of a revocation of a proxy designation shall not affect any vote or act previously taken. Each proxy shall automatically cease upon conveyance of the Lot.

heading: Majority of Owners
text: As used in this Code of Regulations, the term majority shall mean those votes, Owners, Members or other group as the context may indicate totaling more than fifty (50%) percent of the total number.

heading: Quorum
text: Except as otherwise provided in these Code of Regulations or in the Declaration, those Members present, in person or by proxy shall constitute a quorum at all meetings of the Association. Any provision in the Declaration concerning quorums is specifically incorporated herein.

heading: Conduct of Meetings
text: The President shall preside over all meetings of the Association, and the Secretary shall keep the minutes of the meeting and record in the minute book all resolutions adopted, as well as a record of all transactions occurring thereat.

heading: Action Without A Meeting
text: Any action which may be authorized or taken at a meeting of the members, except the election of Board members, may be authorized or taken without a meeting with the affirmative vote or approval, and in writing or writings signed by not less than a majority of the Members. Any such writing shall be entered into the minute book of the Association. Article III — Board of Directors

heading: Governing Body
text: Except as otherwise provided by law, the Articles of Incorporation, the Declaration or this Code of Regulations, all of the authority of the Association shall be exercised by or under the direction of the Board of Directors.

heading: Number and Qualification of Directors
text: The Board of Directors in the Association shall consist of three (3) persons and shall be those named in the Articles of Incorporation or other such person or persons as may be substituted by the Declarant pursuant to Article XIII, Section 13.3. The spouse of an Owner is qualified to act as a Director if both the Owner and the spouse occupy the Lot. If an Owner is not an individual, that Owner may nominate for the Board of Directors any principal, member of a limited liability company, partner, director, officer, or employee of that Owner.

heading: Nomination of Directors
text: Except for Directors selected by the Declarant, nominations for election of the Board of Directors shall be made by a Nominating Committee. The Nominating Committee shall consist of a Chairman, who shall be a member of the Board, and two (2) or more Members of the Association. The Nominating Committee shall be appointed by the Board at each annual meeting of the Members to serve from the close of such annual meeting until the close of the next annual meeting. The Nominating Committee shall make as many nominations for election to the Board as it shall in its discretion determine but in no event less than the number of vacancies or terms to be filled. Nominations shall be permitted from the floor. All candidates shall have a reasonable opportunity to communicate their qualifications to the Members and to solicit votes.

heading: Election of Directors
text: The Directors shall be elected at each annual meeting of the Members of the Association or at a special meeting called for the purpose of electing Directors. At a meeting of Members of the Association at which Directors are to be elected, only persons nominated as candidates shall be eligible for election as Directors and the candidates receiving the greatest number of votes shall be elected. The Board may adopt rules regarding nominations and procedure for elections. Election to the Board shall be by secret written ballot and at such elections, the Members or their proxies may cast, in respect to each vacancy, such voting power as they are entitled to exercise under the provisions of the Declaration.

heading: Term of Office; Resignations
text: Except for those Directors appointed by the Declarant, each Director shall hold office for a term of two (2) years and until his or her successor is elected, or until his or her earlier resignation, removal from office, or death. It is intended by these Code of Regulations that the terms of the Directors shall be staggered with one (1) Director being elected in odd numbered years and two (2) Directors being elected in even numbered years. The initial terms of the Directors elected by the Owners shall be adjusted to carry out this intent. Any Director may resign at any time by oral statement to that effect made at a meeting of the Board of Directors or in writing to that effect delivered to the Secretary of the Association. Such resignation to take effect immediately or at such other time as the Director may specify. In the event of death or resignation of a Director, his or her successor shall be selected by a majority of the remaining members of the Board and shall serve for the unexpired term of the predecessor.

heading: Compensation
text: Members of the Board of Directors shall serve without compensation, except that they may be reimbursed for actual expenses incurred on behalf of the Association.

heading: Removal of Directors
text: Except for those appointed by the Declarant, at any regular or special meeting of the Association duly called, any one or more of the members of the Board of Directors may be removed, with or without cause, by a majority vote of the Owners, and a successor may then and there be elected to fill the vacancy thus created. A Director whose removal has been proposed shall be given at least ten (10) days notice of the calling of the meeting and the purposes thereof and shall be given an opportunity to be heard at the meeting. Additionally, any Director who has three (3) unexcused absences from Board meetings or who is delinquent in payment of an Assessment for more then twenty (20) days may be removed by a majority vote of the Directors at meeting, a quorum being present.

heading: Organization Meetings
text: The first meeting of the members of the Board of Directors following each annual meeting of the Members shall be held within ten (10) days thereafter at such time and place as shall be fixed by the Board.

heading: Regular Meetings
text: Regular meetings of the Board of Directors may be held at such time and place as shall be determined from time to time by a majority of the Directors, but at least four (4) such meetings shall be held during each fiscal year with at least one (1) per quarter.

heading: Special Meetings
text: Special meetings of the Board of Directors shall be held when called by written notice signed by the President or Secretary of the Association, or by any two (2) Directors. The notice shall specify the time and place of the meeting and the nature of any special business to be considered.

heading: Notice of Meetings; Waiver
text: Notice of the time and place of each meeting of the Directors, whether regular or special, shall be given to each Director at least seventy-two (72) hours before the time set for the meeting in accordance with Article VII, Section 7. Waiver of notice of meetings of the Directors shall be deemed the equivalent of proper notice. Any Director may, in writing, waive notice of any meeting of the Board, either before or after the holding of such meeting. Such writing shall be entered into the minutes of the meeting. Attendance of any Director at any meeting without protesting, prior to or at the commencement of at the meeting, the lack of proper notice shall be deemed to be a waiver by him or her of notice of such meeting.

heading: Quorum of the Board of Directors
text: At all meetings of the Board of Directors, a majority of the Directors shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business, and the votes of a majority of the Directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present shall constitute the decision of the Board. A meeting at which a quorum is initially present may continue to transact business, notwithstanding the withdrawal of the Directors, if any action taken is approved by at least a majority of the required quorum for that meeting. Notice of adjournment of a meeting need not be given if the time and place to which it is adjourned are fixed and announced at such meeting. At such adjourned meeting at which a quorum is present, any business which might have been transacted at the meeting originally called may be transacted.

heading: Conduct of Meetings
text: The President shall preside over all meetings of the Board of Directors, and the Secretary shall keep the minutes of the meeting and record in the minute book all resolutions adopted, as well as a record of all transaction occurring thereat.

heading: Open Meetings
text: All meetings of the Board of Directors shall be open to all Members of the Association, but Members other than the Directors may not participate in any discussion or deliberation unless expressly so authorized by a majority of a quorum of the Board.

heading: Executive Session
text: The Board may, with approval of a majority of a quorum, adjourn a meeting and reconvene in executive session to discuss and vote upon personnel matters, litigation in which the Association is or may become involved, or orders of business of similar nature. The nature of any and all business to be considered in executive session shall first be announced in open session.

heading: Action Without A Meeting
text: Any action which may be authorized or taken at a meeting of the Board of Directors may be authorized or taken without a meeting with the affirmative vote or approval, and in writing or writings signed by all the Directors. Any such writing shall be entered into the minute book of the Association. An explanation of the action taken shall be posted at a prominent place or places within the Properties within three (3) days after written consents of all the Board members have been obtained.

heading: Voting By Directors
text: A Director who is present at a meeting of the Board or any committee meeting when corporate action is taken shall be deemed to have assented to the action taken unless: a) He or she objects at the beginning of the meeting (or promptly upon arrival) to holding it or transacting business at the meeting; b) His or her dissent or abstention from the action taken is entered in the minutes of the meeting; or c) He or she delivers written notice of his or her dissent or abstention to the presiding officer of the meeting before its adjournment or to the Corporation immediately after adjournment of the meeting. This right of dissent or abstention shall not be available to a Director who votes in favor of the action taken. Article IV — Officers

heading: Officers
text: The officers of the Association shall be a President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer. The Board of Directors may elect such other officers, including one or more Assistant Secretaries and one or more Assistant Treasurers, as it shall deem desirable, such officers to have the authority and perform the duties prescribed from time to time by the Board. Any two or more offices may be held by the same person, excepting the offices of President and Secretary. The President and Treasurer shall be elected from among members of the Board of Directors.

heading: Election; Term of Office; Vacancies
text: The officers of the Association shall be elected annually by the Board of Directors at the first meeting of the Board following each annual meeting of the Members, as herein set forth in Article III. A vacancy in any office arising because of death, resignation, removal or otherwise may be filled by the Board for the unexpired portion of the term.

heading: Removal
text: Any officer may be removed by the Board of Directors whenever in its judgment the best interests of the Association would be served thereby.

heading: Powers and Duties
text: The officers of the Association shall each have such powers and duties as generally pertain to their respective offices, as well as such powers and duties as may from time to time be specifically conferred or imposed by the Board. The President shall be the chief executive officer of the Association. The Treasurer shall have the primary responsibility for the preparation of the budget and may delegate all or part of the preparation and notification duties to a finance, management agent or both.

heading: Resignation
text: Any officer may resign at any time by giving written notice to the Board of Directors, the President, or the Secretary. Such resignation shall take effect on the date of the receipt of such notice or at any later time specified therein, and unless otherwise specified therein, the acceptance of such resignation shall not be necessary to make it effective. Article V — Committees

heading: General
text: Committees to perform such tasks and to serve for such periods as may be designated by a resolution adopted by a majority of the Directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present are hereby authorized. Such committees shall perform such duties and have such powers as may be provided in the resolution. Each committee be composed as required by law and operate in accordance with the terms of the resolution of the Board designating such committee or with rules adopted by the Board and to the full extent permitted by law.

heading: Executive Committee
text: The Board of Directors may, by resolution adopted or signed by all of the Directors, appoint an Executive Committee to consist of one or more Directors. The Board may delegate any or all of its duties to such committee. Any resolution or writing appointing such committee must acknowledge the responsibility of all of the Directors for the operation and administration of the Association. The Declarant during any Declarant Control Period shall have the right to appoint an Executive Committee and to delegate such duties as the Declarant deems necessary.

heading: Architectural Control Committee
text: The Board of Directors may appoint an Architectural Control Committee which shall be responsible for plan approval in accordance with Article IX of the Declaration. In addition, the committee shall develop and promulgate architectural standards and guidelines with respect to those matters that are within the Association’s authority to regulate. Article VI — Determination and Payment of Assessments

heading: Adoption of Budget
text: It shall be the duty of the Board to prepare and adopt a budget covering the estimated Common Expenses of the Association for the coming fiscal year. The budget shall also include a capital contribution or reserve in accordance with a capital budget separately prepared. After adoption of the budget, the Board shall cause the summary of the budget and the Assessments to be levied against each Lot for the following year to be delivered to each Owner. Such summary shall be delivered at least thirty (30) days prior to the start of the fiscal year. The budget and Assessments shall take effect on the first day of the fiscal year.

heading: Capital Budget and Contribution
text: The Board shall annually prepare a capital budget which shall take into account the number and nature of replaceable assets, the expected life of each asset and the expected repair or replacement cost. The Board shall set the required capital contribution, if any, in an amount sufficient to permit meeting the projected capital needs of the Association, as shown on the capital budget, with respect to both amount and timing by annual assessments over the period of the budget. The capital contribution required shall be fixed by the Board and included within the budget and assessment, as provided in Section 1 of this Article. A copy of the capital budget shall be distributed to each Owner in the same manner as the operating budget.

heading: Petition for Reconsideration of Budget Increase
text: If the Board receives a petition for reconsideration of budget increase as set forth in Article VII, Section 7.8 of the Declaration, then the Board shall forthwith call a special meeting of the Members. At such meeting, the Members in good standing, in person on by proxy, exercising at least sixty-six and two thirds (66 2/3%) percent of voting power of the Association, may vote to reduce the increase by any amount proposed in the petition, but not lower than the previous years budget.

heading: Failure to Adopt Budget
text: The failure or delay of the Board to adopt a budget as provided herein shall not constitute a waiver or release of the obligation of an Owner to pay the Assessments. In such event, the Assessments based upon the budget last adopted shall continue until such time as the Board adopts a new budget.

heading: Computation of Assessments
text: The Assessments for Common Expenses for each Lot shall be determined in accordance with the operating budget and the capital contribution budget as they apply to the various Lots. Unless otherwise determined by the Board, all Assessments shall be charged on an annual basis.

heading: Payment, Delinquency and Acceleration
text: Unless otherwise determined by the Board, all Assessments shall be payable annually. Any installment of an Assessment shall become delinquent if not paid on the due date as established by the Board. With respect to each installment of an Assessment not paid within five (5) days after its due date, the Board may, at its election, require the Owner to pay a reasonable late charge, together with interest at the rate provided in Section 1343.03 of the Ohio Revised Code calculated from the date of delinquency to and including the date full payment is received by the Association. If any installment of an Assessment is not paid within thirty (30) days after its due date, the Board may, at its election, declare all of the unpaid balance of the Assessment for the then current fiscal year, attributable to that Lot, to be immediately due and payable without further demand and may enforce collection of the full Assessment and all charges thereon in any manner authorized by law, the Declaration and these Code of Regulations.

heading: Remedies for Default
text: If an Owner is in default of payment of an Assessment, the Board may authorize collection through any lawful means, including foreclosure of the lien. Interest and all costs of such collection, including but not limited to court costs, lien fees, attorney fees shall be included in the amount due from the Owner and may be collected. The Board may authorize the Association to bid its interest at any foreclosure sale and to acquire, hold, lease, mortgage and convey any Lot. Article VII — Miscellaneous

heading: Fiscal Year
text: The Association may adopt any fiscal year as determined by the Board.

heading: Parliamentary Rules
text: Except as may be modified by Board resolution establishing modified procedures, Robert’s Rules of Order (current edition) shall govern the conduct of Association proceedings when not in conflict with Ohio law, the Articles of Incorporation, the Declaration, or this Code of Regulations.

heading: Conflicts
text: If there are conflicts or inconsistencies between the provisions of Ohio law, the Articles of Incorporation, the Declaration, and these Code of Regulations, the provisions of Ohio law, the Declaration, the Articles of Incorporation, and this Code of Regulations (in that order) shall prevail.

heading: Books and Records
text: Inspection by Members. The membership book, account books and minutes of the Association, the Board and any committee shall be made available for inspection and copying by any Member or by his or her duly appointed representative at any reasonable time and for a purpose reasonably related to his or her interest as a Member at the office of the Association or at such other place within North Royalton, Cuyahoga County, Ohio, as the Board shall prescribe. a. Rules for Inspection. The Board shall establish reasonable rules with respect to: i. notice to be given to the custodian of the records by the Members desiring to make the inspection; ii. hours and days of the week when such inspection may be made; and iii. payment of the cost of reproducing copies requested by a Member. b. Withholding of Books and Records. Communications, books and records may be withheld from examination or copying by Members to the extent that the records concern: i. information that pertains to Property related personnel matters; ii. communications with legal counsel or attorney work product that pertains to pending litigation or other Property related matters; iii. information that pertains to contracts or transactions currently under negotiation, or information that is contained in a contract or other agreement containing confidentiality requirements and that is subject to those requirements; iv. information that relates to matters involving enforcement of Association documents or rules and regulations promulgated pursuant thereto; v. disclosure of information in violation of law; or vi. meeting minutes or other records of an executive session duly called. c. Inspection by Directors. Every Director shall have the absolute right at any reasonable time to inspect all books, records, and documents of the Association and the physical properties owned or controlled by the Association. The right of inspection by a Director includes the right to make extracts and copies of documents at the expense of the Association.

heading: Records of Unit Owners
text: Within thirty days after a Unit Owner obtains a condominium ownership interest, the Unit Owner shall provide the following information in writing to the Association through the Board: a. The home address, home and business mailing addresses, and the home and business telephone numbers of the Unit Owner and all Occupants of the Unit; b. The name, business address and business telephone number of any person who manages the owner’s Unit as an agent of that owner. c. Within thirty days after a change in any information that this section requires, a Unit Owner shall notify the association, through the Board, in writing of the change. When the Board requests, a Unit Owner shall verify or update the information.

heading: Authorized Communications Equipment
text: Authorized communications equipment means any communications equipment which provides a transmission, including, but not limited to, by telephone, telecopy, or any electronic means, from which it can be determined that the transmission was authorized by, and accurately reflects the intention of, the Member or Director involved and, with respect to meetings, allows all persons participating in the meeting to contemporaneously communicate with each other. The Board shall have the right to adopt procedures and guidelines regarding such equipment and its use.

heading: Notices
text: Unless otherwise provided in this Code of Regulations, all notices, demands, bills, statements, or other communications under this Code of Regulations shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given if delivered personally or sent by telegram, by the use of authorized communications equipment, or by United States mail, express mail, or courier service, with postage or fees prepaid: a. if to a Member, at the address which the Member has designated in writing and filed with the Secretary or, if not such address has been designated, at the address of the residence of such Owner; or b. if to the Association, the Board of Directors, or the Managing Agent, at the principal office of the Association or the Managing Agent, if any, or at such other address as shall be designated by the Board with written notice to the Owners. c. In computing the period of time for the giving of a notice required or permitted under the articles, the regulations, or the Bylaws of the Association, or a resolution of its Members or Directors, the day on which the notice is given shall be excluded, and the day when the act for which notice is given is to be done shall be included, unless the instrument calling for the notice otherwise provides. If notice is given by personal delivery or transmitted by telegram, facsimile, telecopy or electronic mail, the notice shall be deemed to have been given when delivered or transmitted. If notice is sent by United States mail, express mail or courier service, the notice shall be deemed to have been given when deposited in the mail or with the courier service. d. A written notice or report delivered as part of a newsletter or other publication regularly sent to the Members shall constitute a written notice or report if addressed or delivered to the Member’s address shown in the Association’s current list of members, or, in the case of Members who are residents of the same household and who have the same address in the Association’s current list of Members, if addressed or delivered to one of such Members at the address appearing on the Association’s current list of Members.

heading: Amendment
text: Except as otherwise provided by law or the Declaration, this Code of Regulations may be amended by a majority of the Owners. During such time as the Declarant has the right to appoint Directors of the Association pursuant to Article XIII, Section 13.3 of the Declaration, the Declarant shall have the right to consent any amendment to this Code of Regulations pursuant to the provisions in the Declaration.

heading: Financial Review
text: A review of the accounts of the Association shall be made annually in the manner as the Board of Directors may decide, provided, however, after having received the Board’s report at the annual meeting, the Owners, by majority vote, may require the accounts of the Association to be audited as a Common Expense by a public accountant. Adopted pursuant to a resolution of the Board of Directors.

heading: Pets and Animals
text: Authority: Declaration Section 9.1.7. Ordinary household pets kept for non-commercial purposes (dogs, cats, caged birds, and similar) are permitted. Keeping, boarding, breeding, or raising livestock, poultry, fowl (including chickens), or any other farm or commercial animals is prohibited. Pets may not be kept or bred for commercial purposes. No external compound cages, kennels, or hutches are permitted. Pets must be leashed or otherwise controlled when outside the owner's lot, including on common areas and open space. Owners are responsible for promptly cleaning up after their pets on any lot or common area. Pets must not be allowed to create a nuisance, including persistent noise, that disturbs other residents (see also Rule 4).

heading: Vehicles, Parking, and Storage
text: Authority: Declaration Section 9.1.6. Recreational vehicles, trailers, campers, boats, and similar large vehicles may be kept on the property only inside garages, except as allowed below. A recreational vehicle or boat may be parked in a driveway for no more than seventy-two (72) consecutive hours, and only for active loading, unloading, cleaning, or maintenance. Commercial trucks bearing logos or racks may be parked on the property only inside garages. No junk, inoperable, or unregistered vehicle (one without current registration plates displayed) may be kept anywhere on the property except inside a garage. Vehicle repairs and vehicle storage are permitted only inside garages. Vehicles may not be parked on lawns, landscaped areas, or common areas.

heading: Trash and Recycling
text: Authority: Declaration Section 9.1.5. No accumulation or outdoor storage of litter, refuse, bulk materials, or trash is permitted on any lot, except in connection with active construction. Trash and recycling containers must be kept out of public view except on collection days. They may be placed at the curb no earlier than the evening before collection and must be returned to their storage location by the end of collection day. Any front-facing bin enclosure must meet the size and materials standards in the Design Guidelines (its construction is an architectural matter). No incinerator or outdoor burning of trash is permitted (see also Declaration Section 9.1.8).

heading: Noise and Nuisance
text: Authority: Declaration Sections 9.1.2 and 9.1.3. No person may create unreasonably loud noise (security devices excepted) or engage in any activity intended to cause annoyance, discomfort, or disturbance to others lawfully present in the community. Residents are asked to keep noise to considerate levels, particularly between 10:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. No emission of dust, odors, or other substances, and no discharge of waste, beyond normal residential activity that adversely affects neighbors' use or comfort.

heading: Holiday and Seasonal Decorations
text: Authority: Board rule under Declaration Section 9.3; reflects community practice. Holiday and seasonal decorations are permitted. Decorations must be removed within forty-five (45) days after the associated holiday. Lighting displays should be considerate of neighbors and must not create a traffic hazard. Music or sound-producing decorations must be operated at reasonable volume levels and are subject to Rule 4. Decorations must not block sidewalks or other public access ways.

heading: Leasing and Occupancy
text: Authority: Declaration Section 1.12 (Dwelling Unit) and Section 9.1.1 (No Trade or Business); Bylaws Article VII, Section 5 (Records of Owners). Each dwelling is intended for use as a single-family residence. No trade or business may be conducted from a lot except as the limited home-occupation exception in Declaration Section 9.1.1 (No Trade or Business) allows. Any lease must be of the entire dwelling unit, and the lease is subject to the Declaration, Bylaws, these Rules, and the Design Guidelines. The owner remains responsible for the conduct of tenants and guests. Within the time the Bylaws require, an owner who leases or sells must provide the Association the owner's and any occupant's contact information and the name and contact of any managing agent.

heading: Common Areas and Open Space
text: Authority: Declaration Sections 4.2.6 (Preservation Easement), 5.6, and 9.1.2. The open space, conservation/preservation easement areas, wetlands, and retention basin must be left in their natural condition. No dumping of yard waste, debris, fill, or any material is permitted in these areas. No cutting, clearing, or chemical treatment of trees, shrubs, or vegetation within preservation-easement areas, and no construction, fences, or structures within them. Nothing may be done that obstructs or alters the surface-water management system (swales, ditches, basins) or changes the approved lot grading.

heading: Architectural-Review Appeals
text: Authority: Board rule under Declaration Section 9.2 and Bylaws Article V, Section 3 (Architectural Control Committee). An owner whose architectural request is denied by the Architectural Control Committee or the Board may appeal to the full Board within thirty (30) days of the decision. Appeals must be in writing and state one or more grounds: new information; consistency with community aesthetics; comparable changes approved elsewhere; undue hardship; or procedural error. The Board will consider the appeal at its next scheduled meeting and issue a written decision within fifteen (15) days. The owner may appear in person. This appeal procedure applies only to architectural-review decisions. Notice and hearing for fines and individual assessments are governed separately by Declaration Section 7.5 and are not changed by this Rule.

heading: Enforcement and Fines
text: Authority: Declaration Sections 7.4, 7.5, and 9.3.1. The Board may enforce these Rules by levying a fine (which is also an individual assessment), abating the violation at the owner's expense, or pursuing legal action, as provided in Declaration Section 9.3. Before imposing a fine, the Board will give the owner written notice and an opportunity to be heard under the procedure in Declaration Section 7.5, except in emergencies or for repeated or continuing violations. The Board may adopt and publish a separate schedule of fine amounts by resolution.

heading: Amendment
text: Authority: Article VI of the Declaration (Powers of the Association). The Board may adopt, amend, or repeal these Rules by resolution at a duly held meeting, without a vote of the owners. Owners will be notified of any new or amended Rule, and the change takes effect on the date the Board sets, after reasonable notice. Adoption These Rules & Regulations were adopted by the Board of Directors of The Villas at Worthington Homeowners Association, Inc. by resolution duly adopted on the ______ day of ________________, 2026, and take effect after reasonable notice to the Owners. ____________________________________ ____________________ President Date ____________________________________ ____________________ Secretary Date Appendix A — Schedule of Fines (Proposed) This schedule is proposed for adoption by separate Board resolution under Section 9.3 and Section 6.3.13 of the Declaration. The amounts below are starting examples for the Board to set or adjust. All fines are individual assessments and are subject to the written-notice and hearing procedure in Declaration Section 7.5 before they are imposed. First occurrence of a violation: written notice and an opportunity to cure (no fine). Failure to cure, or a second occurrence of the same violation: $25. Third occurrence, or continued violation: $50. Each additional 30-day period the violation continues after notice: $100. Health, safety, or continuing violations may be abated by the Association at the Owner's expense under Section 9.3, in addition to any fine. The Board may waive, reduce, or increase any amount, and may adopt a different schedule by resolution.

heading: General Guidelines Applicable to All Homes
text: House Placement and Yard Grading All dwelling units must conform to existing grade and drainage patterns. Builders are responsible for regrading the lot to meet the approved drainage plan. Preserve natural woods where practical. Home Placement Rules A minimum of one different house type elevation must separate identical models side by side. Identical elevations are allowed across the street or at intersecting lot lines. On a cul-de-sac, adjacent homes cannot share the same elevation.

heading: Dwelling Type and Size
text: Permitted Dwelling Types One-story homes with or without a basement. Story-and-a-half or Cape Cod homes (upper level within roof gables with dormers). Two-story homes with or without a basement. Minimum Sizes 1,200 sq. ft. for one-story dwellings. 1,300 sq. ft. for two-story dwellings. Minor variances up to 10% below minimum size requirements may be permitted at the Board’s discretion based on lot size and neighborhood character.

heading: Roof and Garages
text: Roofs Dwelling roof and gable pitch: Minimum 6:12. Porch/patio roof pitch: Minimum 3.5:12. All shingles must be a uniform color. Garages Attached two-car minimum garages required for new construction.

heading: Yards, Driveways, and Walks
text: Landscaping Front yards must be landscaped within 90 days of occupancy (weather permitting). Rear yards extend behind the rear elevation to the property lines. Driveways and Walks Permitted materials include: Concrete (plain or decorative) Brick, concrete, or stone pavers Restrictions: Gravel, dirt, or asphalt driveways are not permitted. Driveways must not extend beyond front elevation into side lot areas. Setbacks: At least 2 feet from lot lines; walks must be within 6 feet of dwelling side.

heading: Color Schemes and Exterior Finishes
text: Siding Colors No two adjacent homes may have the same siding color. Allowed on opposite sides of street or intersecting lot lines. Cul-de-sacs may have intersecting homes with same color. Vinyl siding colors must be approved with submitted sample. Trim, Shutters, Doors Uniform trim color on all architectural elements of a single home. Door and shutter colors must be from the following color families in relation to the main siding color: Neutral colors (white, black, gray, beige, or brown) Colors from the same palette as the siding but in a contrasting shade Traditional accent colors appropriate to the architectural style of the home Colors matching other architectural elements of the home, such as stone or brick accents Stone and Masonry Finishes Stone, brick, and other masonry elements are permitted in colors that complement the home’s overall design scheme. No specific restrictions on stone or brick colors as long as the general siding color rules are followed. Masonry elements should be consistently applied across all visible elevations of the structure where used as a design feature. Transitions between siding and masonry materials should occur at inside corners where possible, rather than mid-wall.

heading: Prohibited Structures and Exterior Modifications
text: New Construction Restrictions Underground homes and log homes are prohibited. Exterior Modifications No porches, additions, or appendages unless matching original home in material, style, and color. Must be fully integrated into home design. Above-grade structures must be enclosed to grade. Storage Restrictions Front porches may only contain standard porch furniture. No visible exterior carpet from the street. Front-facing trash and recycling bin storage enclosures are permitted if they meet the following: Located immediately outside the garage or along the driveway side of the home, but not projecting forward of the main front elevation line of the garage. Must be fully enclosed within a structure no larger than 4 feet high, 4 feet wide, and 3 feet deep. Materials must match or complement the home exterior (e.g., neutral siding or painted wood). Pets and Animals The keeping of animals is a use restriction, not an architectural standard. It is governed by Section 9.1.7 of the Declaration and by the Association’s Rules & Regulations, not by these Design Guidelines.

heading: Outdoor Equipment and Fixtures
text: Railings Must be wood, composite, or wrought iron look in a complementary color. Solar Panels In accordance with Ohio Revised Code § 5312.16, homeowners have the right to install solar panels. While the HOA Board may establish reasonable guidelines regarding the placement of solar energy systems, it cannot prohibit them outright or impose restrictions that significantly increase the cost or decrease the efficiency of the system. Homeowners planning to install solar panels must submit detailed plans including: Panel specifications Installation method Placement location Visual impact mitigation measures, which may include: Low-profile mounting systems Panel placement that aligns with roof planes where technically feasible Color-coordinated components and frames when available without significant cost increase Chimneys Metal flues must be enclosed. Direct-vent chimneys must vent to rear or side. Water Discharge Must comply with the subdivision’s approved drainage and city regulations. Skylights Permitted on rear-facing roofs. Other placements may be approved for contemporary designs.

heading: Pools, Spas, and Play Equipment
text: Pools Only in-ground pools are permitted (no above-ground or semi-in-ground pools). Kiddie pools (temporary) allowed up to 72 hours. In-ground pools must: Be approved by Board. Be at least 10 feet from any property line. Not obstruct surface water flow. Include screening (landscaping/decking). Be fenced per city code and Section 11 of these guidelines; fencing must not attach to pool. Hot Tubs/Spas Hot tubs and spas are permitted in the rear yard. Units may be in-ground, or above ground if incorporated into a deck, consistent with the Declaration. A standalone above-ground hot tub or spa not incorporated into a deck is not permitted. All hot tubs and spas must be screened using fencing, landscaping, or another board-approved method to reduce visibility from the street and adjacent lots. Units must comply with side and rear setback requirements. Play Equipment All play equipment must be placed in the rear yard. Equipment must not violate property setback lines. Equipment must be constructed of wood or painted/stained in natural tones (gray/brown/white). Deck integration is permitted but not required. Equipment must be properly maintained and in good condition. Basketball Hoops All basketball hoops (fixed or portable) must have a clear, professional-style backboard and be maintained in good condition. Goals must not be attached to the dwelling or garage. Placement must be behind the front elevation of the house or, in the case of corner lots, at least 15 feet from the street-side setback. Broken or damaged goals must be repaired or removed promptly. Portable hoops do not need to be put away after use but must follow all placement and maintenance rules.

heading: Outbuildings and Storage Structures
text: Sheds and Pool Pump Buildings Sheds allowed up to 160 sq. ft. and 10 ft. in height, subject to City of North Royalton zoning limits, which control if more restrictive (per Section 9.1.1 of the Declaration). Must match house exterior with the following specific requirements: Roof pitch must be at least 4:12 Roofing shingles must be identical in color and style to the main house Siding material must be the same type and color as the main house Trim color must be the same as the main house trim Must be on a concrete pad and 10 feet from any property line.

heading: HVAC and Utilities
text: AC Units and Heat Pumps Must be placed in side or rear yard. Screening of AC units and heat pumps is encouraged but not required. If homeowners choose to screen their units, recommended methods include: Landscaping that is at least the height of the unit Fencing or lattice that matches or complements the home’s exterior Manufactured HVAC screens designed for this purpose Units should be maintained in good working order and kept free of excessive rust or deterioration visible from neighboring properties.

heading: Fencing
text: Permitted Styles No chain link fences. Allowed only in rear yard. Split rail (2–3 rail, up to 5’) with optional dog wire. Vinyl, PVC, or aluminum picket fences (max 4’). Wood, vinyl, or PVC privacy fences (max 6’). Setback & Variance No fences within street-side setback (corner lots). Up to 4’ extension from side of home allowed for side-door access. Pool fencing must meet city code (cross-reference with Section 8 pool requirements). Approval Criteria The Board will evaluate fence approval requests based on the following specific criteria: Compliance with material, style, and height requirements Appropriate placement within authorized areas Quality of materials and professional installation plan Impact on drainage and utility easements Visual cohesiveness with surrounding properties Maintenance All fences must be maintained in good repair, structurally sound, and in a condition consistent with their original appearance, including repainting, re-staining, or repair of damaged sections as needed.

heading: Antennas, Satellite Dishes, and Communications Equipment
text: Protected Communications Equipment In accordance with the FCC’s Over-the-Air Reception Devices (OTARD) Rule, homeowners have the right to install: Satellite dishes ≤ 1 meter diameter TV broadcast antennas MMDS/LMDS antennas ≤ 1 meter (wireless cable/internet reception equipment) Internet or broadband antennas ≤ 1 meter Placement Where possible, equipment should be placed in rear yard or rear of dwelling where not visible from street. Equipment may be placed where needed for optimal signal reception, even if visible from the street. When multiple placement options would provide adequate reception, the least visibly intrusive location is preferred. Maintenance & Aesthetics Must be painted/screened to blend in if possible, provided such requirements do not impair reception or impose unreasonable costs. Must be removed if not in use.

heading: Landscaping and Lot Maintenance
text: Holiday Decorations Holiday and seasonal decorations are a temporary-display and conduct matter rather than a permanent architectural standard. They are addressed in the Association’s Rules & Regulations. Landscaping Requirements Landscaping and regular lawn maintenance required. Street-facing sides must have raised beds with mulch and shrubs. Lot Cleanliness Lots must be kept free of debris. Fill material may only be dumped within 5 days of construction. Association may charge owners for non-compliance. Grading Must follow City-approved plans. Any changes require city approval. Maintenance Homeowners must ensure that all required landscaping (e.g., shrubs, mulch, raised beds) is properly maintained, healthy, and refreshed as necessary to prevent deterioration or a neglected appearance.

heading: Vehicle Parking and Storage
text: Parking Restrictions Vehicle parking and storage are matters of property use, not architecture. They are governed by Section 9.1.6 of the Declaration and the Association’s Rules & Regulations, not by these Design Guidelines.

heading: Exterior Lighting and House Numbers
text: Lighting Please choose fixtures with moderate brightness appropriate for residential areas. Light fixtures should be positioned to primarily illuminate your own property. Be mindful of neighbors when positioning lights to avoid direct illumination into adjacent windows. House Numbers Must be visible from the street. Minimum number height: 4 inches. Must be in a contrasting color to the background.

heading: Exterior Paint and Maintenance
text: All dwellings must be maintained in good repair. The Board may require owners to repaint, clean, or make necessary exterior repairs when any of the following conditions are present: Peeling, chipping, or faded paint covering more than 10% of any exterior surface Broken, missing, or damaged siding, trim, gutters, or downspouts Visible rot or damage to wood components Cracked or damaged masonry Roof damage or excessive wear Mold, mildew, or algae growth visible from the street or neighboring properties

heading: Flags and Signage
text: Flags In accordance with Ohio Revised Code § 5301.072, homeowners have the right to display: The United States flag State of Ohio flag United States armed forces service flags POW/MIA flag Flag displays must comply with the U.S. Flag Code (4 U.S.C. §§ 5-10), which includes: Proper illumination if displayed at night Respectful handling and display Proper positioning when displayed with other flags Flags may be mounted on the home with appropriate brackets or displayed on a freestanding pole not to exceed 20 feet in height. Signage Political signs may be displayed during election seasons (90 days before and 10 days after an election). Signs may not exceed 4 square feet in size. Real estate “For Sale” signs are permitted but limited to one per property. Contractor signs may only be displayed while work is actively being performed and must be removed upon completion. Home security system signs are permitted if modest in size (not exceeding 1 square foot).

heading: Accessibility Modifications
text: Reasonable Accommodations In compliance with the Fair Housing Act and Ohio law, the Association recognizes homeowners’ rights to make reasonable modifications to their property when necessary to afford disabled residents full enjoyment of the premises. Modifications that would otherwise violate these Design Guidelines may be permitted when needed for accessibility purposes. Common Examples of Accessibility Modifications: Ramps for wheelchair access Widened doorways Grab bars and handrails Modified landscaping to accommodate mobility needs Accessible parking spaces or driveway modifications Sensory accommodations such as specialized lighting Submission Process Homeowners should submit plans for such modifications to the Management Company/Board with the following documentation: Detailed description of the proposed modification Professional plans or drawings Statement of need from a healthcare provider (without disclosing private medical details) Proposed contractor information if applicable

heading: Appeals Process and Dispute Resolution
text: Appeals Process An owner whose architectural request is denied may appeal to the full Board under the procedure set out in the Association’s Rules & Regulations. That appeal procedure applies only to architectural-review decisions; notice and hearing for fines and individual assessments are governed separately by Section 7.5 of the Declaration.

heading: Variance, Discretion, and Modifications to Guidelines
text: Governing Document Hierarchy These Design Guidelines are adopted by the Villas at Worthington Homeowners Association, which operates as a planned community under the Ohio Planned Community Act (R.C.5312). These guidelines are subordinate to and must be read in conjunction with the Association's Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (CC&Rs) and the Bylaws. In the event of a conflict, the CC&Rs and the Bylaws shall control. Where these Guidelines are silent on a matter, or are less restrictive than the Declaration, the Declaration governs. These Guidelines may impose standards that are equal to or stricter than the Declaration and may address matters on which the Declaration is silent, but they cannot permit what the Declaration prohibits or prohibit what the Declaration permits. Any change requiring those results must be made by amending the Declaration itself under Section 14.2. For any use or improvement not addressed in these Guidelines, owners should consult the Declaration. Discretion The elected HOA Board has discretion over guideline interpretations, subject to the appeals process outlined in Section 19. Variances May be granted if not detrimental to neighboring lots and in community’s best interest. Precedent from previously granted variances may be considered but does not guarantee approval of similar requests. Right to Modify Guidelines may be updated by the Board, provided changes maintain the first-class character of the development. Any substantial changes to these guidelines will be communicated to all homeowners with at least 30 days notice before implementation.

heading: The community, in brief
text: Villas of Worthington is a 114-unit planned community (PUD) in North Royalton, Cuyahoga County, Ohio, established in 2007. The Association — Villas at Worthington Homeowners Association, Inc., an Ohio nonprofit corporation — is self-managed by an elected, all-volunteer Board of Directors rather than an outside management company.

heading: Dues
text: Annual dues are $400 per unit ($33.33/month), unchanged since 2020. Pay assessments and manage your account through the Resident Portal (PayHOA), linked from the homepage — it's the fastest, self-service way to check your balance or pay.

heading: The Board
text: Three elected seats — President, Treasurer, Secretary — each serving staggered terms. Current officers and their terms are listed on the About page. Board meetings are open to all Members (Bylaws §14); non-Director Members may not participate in Board discussion or deliberation unless the Board expressly authorizes it, and the Board may adjourn into executive session for matters like personnel or pending litigation (Bylaws §15). Reach the Board at board@villasofworthingtonhoa.com for anything not covered by PayHOA.

heading: Architectural review (ARC)
text: Before any exterior construction, alteration, or modification — additions, fences, patios, sheds, paint/siding changes, landscaping changes, and similar work — submit an ARC Request through the form on the website. Under Declaration §9.2.1, the Board (holding the original plan-approval authority described there, per §9.2.1.3) will approve, reject, or modify a complete request in writing within 30 days after acknowledging receipt; if you don't hear back in that time, the request is deemed approved — though any work must still conform to the Declaration, the Design Guidelines, and applicable City of North Royalton codes and permits. Full architectural standards are in the Design Guidelines (Documents page).

heading: Quick rules reference
text: Summarized from the Rules & Regulations, adopted by the Board in 2026 — which cite the exact Declaration section behind each one; see that document for full text. Pets — ordinary household pets (dogs, cats, caged birds) are fine; no livestock, poultry, or commercial breeding. Leash or otherwise control pets outside your lot, and clean up after them. Parking — RVs, trailers, boats, and campers stay in garages, with a 72-hour driveway exception for active loading/cleaning. No junk or unregistered vehicles outside a garage; no parking on lawns or common areas. Trash & recycling — containers stay out of public view except on collection day; curb placement no earlier than the evening before, back to storage by end of collection day. No outdoor burning. Leasing — whole-unit leases only, subject to all governing documents; owners remain responsible for tenants and must give the Association contact info for any lease or sale. Common areas & open space — ponds, wetlands, and preservation easements stay in natural condition; no dumping, clearing, or altering the surface-water/drainage system.

heading: Insurance & the reserve fund
text: The Association carries liability, crime, and common-area property coverage — see the Insurance Summary (Documents page) for types and limits. Importantly, that coverage does not insure individual dwellings: as in most single-family PUDs (unlike a condominium), each owner needs their own homeowner's policy for their unit's structure, contents, and personal liability. Separately, a professionally studied reserve fund pays for major shared-property replacements (ponds, the paved trail, mailboxes, fencing, entry features) — see the Finances page for the current balance and funding plan.

heading: Where everything else lives
text: This packet summarizes the highlights — no need to separately download anything it already covers. Beyond that: Documents has the full Declaration, Bylaws, Rules & Regulations, Design Guidelines, maps, Reserve Study, and Insurance Summary (with a search box); Minutes has approved Board meeting minutes; Finances has dues, spending history, and reserve detail; Contact has the Board's email, mailing address, and what to reach out about. Questions this packet doesn't answer? Email the Board at board@villasofworthingtonhoa.com.

heading: What the Association's policies cover
text: The Association's coverage is carried across two linked “Residential Community Association” policies (covering different common-area locations within the community) plus a separate crime bond. Each Residential Community Association policy carries the liability limits below; see “What it doesn't cover” for the property side. Coverage Limit (each policy, unless noted) General/Business Liability $2,000,000 per occurrence General Aggregate $4,000,000 Products/Completed Operations Aggregate $4,000,000 Medical Expenses (any one person) $5,000 Damage to Premises Rented to You $300,000 Directors & Officers Liability $2,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate Employee Dishonesty (Crime) $25,000 Computer Equipment (Inland Marine) $10,000 Loss of Income & Extra Expense $10,000 In addition, a separate Fidelity Bond covers the Association against theft or dishonesty by anyone who handles Association funds, at a $55,000 limit.

heading: Common-area property covered
text: The Association's policies insure the shared physical structures it owns — entry signs, lamp posts, and mailbox structures — along with the business personal property associated with them, plus two additional scheduled items. Basic deductible: $1,000. Special deductibles apply to money/securities and employee dishonesty ($250 each) and equipment breakdown ($1,000).

heading: What it does not cover
text: This is the part every owner should know: the Association's policy does not insure individual dwelling units. Villas of Worthington is a single-family planned community (PUD), not a condominium — unlike a condo association, which typically insures the building shells, each homeowner here is individually responsible for insuring their own home's structure, contents, and personal liability (a standard HO-3 homeowner's policy or equivalent). The Association's coverage exists for common areas and the Association's own liability and operations, not as a substitute for your own homeowner's insurance. Questions about coverage? Contact the Board at board@villasofworthingtonhoa.com.
